Evaluate a cognitive model or fitted model

Source: R/S7-generics.R, R/S7-methods.R, R/S7-stanfit-methods.R
evaluate_model.Rd

Evaluates the predictions of a cognitive model or fitted Stan model against observed categorization responses. When applied to fitted model objects with attached test data (such as MVBU_Stanfit or MVBU_StanfitPosterior), leaving x = NULL and response_category = NULL automatically evaluates the model against the model's attached test data.

Usage

evaluate_model(
  model,
  x = NULL,
  response_category = NULL,
  method = "log_lik",
  decision_rule = if (identical(method, "accuracy")) "criterion" else "proportional",
  return_by_x = FALSE,
  ...
)

## S7 method for class <MVBU_CognitiveModel>
evaluate_model(
  model,
  x = NULL,
  response_category = NULL,
  method = "log_lik",
  decision_rule = if (identical(method, "accuracy")) "criterion" else "proportional",
  return_by_x = FALSE,
  ...
)

## S7 method for class <MVBU_Stanfit>/<MVBU_StanfitPosterior>
evaluate_model(
  model,
  x = NULL,
  response_category = NULL,
  method = "log_lik",
  decision_rule = if (identical(method, "accuracy")) "criterion" else "proportional",
  return_by_x = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

model

A cognitive model object (e.g., MVG_IdealObserver, NIW_IdealAdaptor) or MVBU_Stanfit.

x

Observations/stimuli (matrix, data frame, list of numeric vectors, or numeric vector). If NULL and model has attached test data (e.g., MVBU_Stanfit or MVBU_StanfitPosterior), stimuli x are automatically extracted from the model's attached test data.

response_category

Vector of observed category responses for each observation. If NULL and model has attached test data (e.g., MVBU_Stanfit or MVBU_StanfitPosterior), responses are automatically extracted from the model's attached test data column "response".

method

Evaluation method(s): "log_lik" (default), "log_lik_permutation_constant", "accuracy", or "likelihood-up-to-constant" (deprecated alias). Can be a character vector to return multiple metrics.

decision_rule

Decision rule to apply: "proportional", "criterion", or "sampling". Defaults to "criterion" when method == "accuracy", and "proportional" otherwise.

return_by_x

Logical; if TRUE, returns evaluation metrics grouped by unique stimulus values \(x\). Defaults to FALSE.

...

Additional arguments passed to methods.

Value

A numeric scalar, a tibble (if return_by_x = TRUE), or a named list of these if multiple methods were requested.

Details

Supported evaluation methods include:

  • "log_lik": Trial-by-trial categorical log-likelihood (default): $$\log L_{\text{cat}} = \sum_{i=1}^N \log P(Y = y_i \mid X = x_i) = \sum_{u=1}^U \sum_{j=1}^K n_{u,j} \log p_{u,j}$$ where \(u\) indexes unique stimulus locations, \(j\) indexes categories, \(n_{u,j}\) is the count of responses for category \(j\) at stimulus \(u\), and \(p_{u,j}\) is the model's predicted probability of category \(j\) at \(u\). This represents the log probability of observing the exact sequence of individual responses \((y_1, \dots, y_N)\). This is the standard likelihood metric in GLMs, logistic regression, and Bayesian Stan models.

  • "accuracy": Proportion of correct / matching responses.

  • "likelihood-up-to-constant": Deprecated alias for "log_lik" (supported until version 0.1).

Additionally, the following method is available to support calculation of order invariant log-likelihoods:

  • "log_lik_permutation_constant": The log multinomial combinatorial permutation factor: $$C = \sum_{u=1}^U \left( \log(N_u!) - \sum_{j=1}^K \log(n_{u,j}!) \right) = \sum_{u=1}^U \log \binom{N_u}{n_{u,1}, \dots, n_{u,K}}$$ where \(N_u = \sum_j n_{u,j}\) is the total number of presentations at stimulus location \(u\). This factor accounts for all permutations of response order at each stimulus location. Crucially, \(C\) depends purely on the observed data and is completely independent of the cognitive model.

Examples

mod <- example_mvg_ideal_observer(n_cues = 2)
x_stim <- matrix(c(10, -1, 55, 0.5), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)
evaluate_model(
  mod,
  x = x_stim,
  response_category = c("/b/", "/k/"),
  method = "log_lik"
)
